title: Digital vs Analog
summary: Electronic signals talk to the Arduino in two different ways:

steps.title: Digital vs Analog
steps.markdownContent: A button can give a digital HIGH or LOW reading. A knob can give changing voltages that the Uno measures as numbers. The voltage is smooth; the ADC reading is a set of steps.

quickCheck.question: A standard light switch is either flipped ON or flipped OFF. Is this digital or analog?
quickCheck.explanation: Digital signals have only two states (ON or OFF), just like a regular light switch!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Digital means two simple choices: ON or OFF, HIGH or LOW. Think of a simple light switch.

quickCheck.question: A volume knob turns smoothly from whisper-quiet to super loud. Is that digital or analog?
quickCheck.explanation: Because the volume changes smoothly through many levels in between, it is an analog signal!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Analog signals can be any level in between, like sliding a volume bar up and down.

steps.title: HIGH/LOW vs. Continuous Waves
steps.markdownContent: The Uno’s analog input turns a voltage into a number from 0 to 1023. Digital HIGH is a recognized logic state; it is not a promise that the pin is exactly 5 volts.

steps.title: Interactive Signal Inspector & Prediction
steps.markdownContent: Flip the virtual switch and move the slider. Predict how the reading changes before you test it.

steps.title: Digital vs Analog Checkpoint
steps.markdownContent: Test your mastery of digital switches and analog waves!

interactiveConfig.question: What does the Uno do with a changing voltage on an analog input?
options: Uses it to power a motor
interactiveConfig.explanation: The Uno measures the voltage and reports a number from 0 to 1023.

learningGoal: Tell a two-state digital signal from a changing analog signal.
